description: Class 1 (READ) — the READ siblings of the mine family, the other half of D-409's decided split. forge.mine.capture@1 (EXTERNAL_MUTATION) is the ONE filesystem seam and lives in plugins/forge-mine-capture/; THIS plugin holds the three READ ops (forge.mine.verify@1, forge.mine.diff@1, forge.mine.list@1) and touches no filesystem at all: reading a foreign tree is the capture seam's consent-gated job, and doing it here would put the highest-risk act in the system behind an ungated READ op. All three ops consume the capture receipt AS STORED — the append-only row forge.mine.capture@1 wrote to vault ns proposal under the content-derived id `mine:<repo>/<rootHash>`, which this plugin re-derives from the mine id's own pin (capture refuses unless pin == rootHash, so the two derivations agree by construction, and their agreement is asserted on the live receipt). verify re-walks the RECEIPT (never the disk) and returns the pack.builder ProofReport@1; diff returns the same shape as an AGREEMENT verdict over two receipts; list enumerates the pinned mines the ledger holds and returns none of their bytes. Refuses by NAME: malformed payload, unpinned mine id, a receipt that is not there, a stored row that is not an object, a receipt-prefixed row whose id names no pin, and a closed ledger. A receipt that EXISTS but disagrees is a failing proof report, never a refusal — including the un-pinned-hash case D-409 names. Reads only: it appends nothing to ns proposal or anywhere else, requests no mutation capability, and needs no law self-check (LAW_POLICY_V1 classifies READ as allow/unjournaled).

contract.doc: verify {mineId} → ProofReport@1 (pack.builder) — re-derives a stored capture receipt from its OWN rows and checks the pin. Loads the single receipt row forge.mine.capture@1 appended to vault ns proposal at the content-derived id `mine:<repo>/<rootHash>`, re-derived here from the mine id's own pin. The 'receipt vs re-walk' of packs/builder/contract/forge-ops.md is a re-walk of the RECEIPT, not of the disk: reading a foreign tree is the EXTERNAL_MUTATION seam's job (D-409) and this plugin has no filesystem capability. Checks, each carrying its own diff: receipt-is-capture-receipt-1, receipt-mine-id-matches-request, file-count-matches-files, files-path-ordered-and-unique, root-hash-recomputes, mine-pin-matches-root-hash, row-id-matches-root-hash, cas-ref-is-content-address, captured-at-is-utc-iso. `replayHash` is the hash this re-walk produced. `result` is pass ⟺ every check passes. Refuses only when there is nothing to verify (malformed payload, unpinned mineId, no such receipt, a stored row that is not an object, a closed ledger); a receipt that exists but disagrees is a FAILING REPORT, not a refusal.

diff {mineA, mineB} → ProofReport@1 (pack.builder) — the file-set delta between two stored capture receipts. Each side is loaded by the same content-derived id and put through the same re-walk verify@1 runs, so a tampered receipt surfaces on left-/right-receipt-verified instead of silently contributing paths. Checks: left-receipt-verified, right-receipt-verified, added, removed, changed — the last three carry their paths in `diff`, capped with an explicit '+N more' so truncation is visible rather than silent. `result` is an AGREEMENT verdict, not a health check: pass ⟺ both receipts verified AND describe the same paths with identical hashes (the 'detect' half of the mine loop, OMEGA-ENDSTATE-VISION). `replayHash` is null by construction — nothing is replayed here; forge.proof.replay@1 owns replay. Refuses only when there is nothing to compare.

list {} → {schemaVersion, op, namespace, count, mines[{ref, mineId, rootHash, rowId, rev}]} — the pinned mines the ledger holds. The payload grammar is CLOSED and EMPTY: the frozen wire pins `{}` (packs/builder/contract/forge-ops.md); an absent payload is that empty object and anything else refuses by name. One vault.query@1 over ns proposal with idPrefix `mine:` enumerates the receipt rows, and each row's id re-derives a MINE_ID (`mine:<repo>/<rootHash>` → `<repo>@<rootHash>`) — which IS the pin, so a pinned mine is fully described by its id and no per-row get is issued. `ref` is the EVIDENCE_REF `mine:<repo>@<pin>` form. This op deliberately returns no file rows: the frozen table assigns `{mineId} → inventory rows` to forge.survey.run@1, and this lane has no seam to read bytes through (D-409 SF2, snapshot bytes undecided). A receipt-prefixed row whose id names no pin is REFUSED (MINE_ROW_ID_MALFORMED), never skipped — corruption is not a row to drop.

capabilities.justification: Two read-only ports, both over vault ns `proposal`, and nothing else. port:vault.get@1 reads the ONE capture-receipt row that verify@1 and diff@1 verify (by content-derived id) — the receipt is read from the governed ledger, never imported across plugin boundaries and never taken from the foreign tree. port:vault.query@1 is the single enumeration list@1 needs to answer `{}` → pinned mines: one idPrefix query over ns proposal, from which each pinned mine is re-derived from its own row id, so no per-row read is issued. Both ports are READ-class in the vault's own manifest and neither can write: this plugin requests NO mutation capability and NO filesystem capability of any kind, which is what keeps D-409's class split honest — the filesystem seam is forge.mine.capture@1's alone (EXTERNAL_MUTATION, consent-gated). It appends nothing to ns proposal: the rows there are capture's, read-only here. No port:law.check@1 either — READ classifies as allow/unjournaled in LAW_POLICY_V1, so the host never gates these ops and an in-handler self-check would be theatre.
